scope.notes: Inventory in progress (124 rows). Covers Exalted: The Fair Folk's Chapter Three character-creation overview (separately for noble and common raksha, since the two follow different Attribute/Background baselines), the four base castes (Diplomat/Entertainer/Warrior/Worker) with their Caste Abilities/Grace/Controlling Grace/Associations/Sobriquets, the twelve named noble hybrid castes (ascendant/shadowed caste pairings), the five Graces (Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword/Heart) with full dot tables plus their general forging rules, the Bedlam mechanic (the raksha's Limit-Trait analog) including all four Virtue-specific Curses and their Lures, the five new Fair Folk Backgrounds (Birth, Freehold, Gossamer, Retinue, Style), the altered Backgrounds (Artifact, Familiar, Manse, Backing/Contacts/Influence) and the excluded ones (Followers, Resources), a set of core signature mechanics (innate Wyld-damage immunity, Craft (Glamour), Wyld stunts/bonuses, Gossamer-and-Glamour Charm fuel, Mutation, Shaping Actions/Reality Shaping, Shaping Combat basics, Oaths, Cold-Wrought Iron), three of Chapter Five's five per-Grace Charm trees in full -- the Heart Grace tree (Nirguna, the Heart -- Name Charms, Bedlam-Influencing Charms, Dodge Charms, Resistance Charms; 14 Charm rows, pp. 155-159/PDF 156-160), the Staff Grace tree (Nirvikalpa, the Staff -- the Laughing Monster Style combat tree plus the separate Society-Forging Charms tree; 12 Charm rows, pp. 193-196/PDF 194-197), and the Cup Grace tree (Dharma, the Cup -- Cup Combat Charms including the named 'Spirit-Twisting Obsession Style' sub-tree, Feeding Charms, Addiction Charms, World-Shaping Charms, Virtue-Shaping Charms; 48 Charm rows, pp. 159-171/PDF 160-172) -- and now the first named sub-section of the fourth tree: the Ring Grace tree's Ring Combat Charms (Nirvishesha, the Ring; 16 Charm rows, pp. 171-175/PDF 172-176). The rest of the Ring Grace tree (All-Consuming God-Monster Style, Body-Strengthening Charms, Creation-Based Crafting, and a large Glamour Charms section including the Forging-the-Grace and Freehold-anchoring Charms), the Sword (Nishkriya) Grace Charm tree, the universal Assumption-type Charm tree (Nirakara, the Mask), Glamour Sorcery, Wyld Artifacts, Adjurations, Behemoths, the apparent sixth 'Way' Grace (Nirupadhika) noted just before Chapter Six, Chapter One's Rakshastan geography/setting material, and Chapter Six's Mountain Folk (a separate playable-adjacent race) are not yet inventoried.

sources.role: Primary Fair Folk (raksha) rules, character creation, Graces, Backgrounds, shaping magic, and setting material

rulesNotes: This PDF has a real, selectable text layer (confirmed via direct PyMuPDF text extraction on multiple sample pages); it is not image-only like the Lunar/Abyssal source PDFs. Text was extracted directly and cross-checked by visually rendering and reading a sample of pages (character-creation summary tables, Grace dot tables, Background dot tables, the Noble Castes pages, and the Storyteller-only 'unshaped' Charm-suggestion sidebar) with the same render-pdf-pages.py + Read-tool workflow used for image-based books, since dot-rating tables and sidebar boxes are exactly the layout that can scramble during plain text extraction. No scrambling was found in the sampled pages; the extracted text order matched the visual layout in every spot-checked case.

Printed page numbers in this book run exactly 1 less than the PDF (physical) page number for the copy used to build this inventory (PDF page = printed page + 1); both are recorded on every citation. This was confirmed both from the Table of Contents (printed page 7, PDF page 8) and from directly reading the printed folio number embedded in the extracted text of dozens of sampled pages.

Fair Folk (raksha) are structurally unlike Solar/Abyssal/Dragon-Blooded/Lunar creation: there are no Attributes-and-Abilities-only Charms, no five Castes shared uniformly by common and noble characters, and no single universal Limit-Trait analog. Common raksha have one feeding Virtue/Grace/caste; noble raksha have two (an 'ascendant' and a 'shadowed' caste), and the ascendant/shadowed pairing across the four base castes produces twelve distinct named noble-caste archetypes (Anarch, Luminary, Panjandrum, Artisan, Courtier, Xia, Eshu, Imperial Raksha, Strategos, Scribe, Ornamental Raksha, Cataphract). Charms are keyed to five Grace Traits (Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword/Heart) rather than to Attributes or Abilities. The Limit-Trait role is filled by Bedlam, which is Virtue-specific rather than universal: each of the four Virtues has its own named Curse (Hubris/Compassion, Namelessness/Conviction, Alienation/Temperance, Meekness-or-Terror/Valor) with its own trigger and recovery condition, plus a mandatory Lure once any Virtue reaches 3+.

'Heart's Blood' does not appear anywhere in this book as Fair Folk terminology; the raksha's core existential Trait is instead the Heart Grace (fixed rating, not freely purchasable), and their wealth/Charm-fuel resource is called Gossamer, not Heart's Blood. No conflation with the Lunar Exalted's unrelated use of similar terms was found or assumed.

Common raksha and noble raksha are covered as two separate character-creation-overview rows in this inventory (fair-folk-creation-overview-common and fair-folk-creation-overview-noble) rather than one combined row, because the book presents them as two materially different baselines (0-dot vs. 3-dot starting Attributes, 0 vs. 10 free Background dots, 1 vs. 3 Favored Abilities, a cheaper Specialty cost for commoners, a cheaper Major Grace cost for nobles) with two separate condensed summary boxes, not one shared creation track with minor caste variation.

Chapter Five's Charm material (pp. 129-213/PDF 130-214, immediately before Chapter Six: The Mountain Folk starts at printed p. 213/PDF 214) is far larger than a single pass can cover: after the general-rules content already inventoried (gossamer/glamour, mutation, shaping actions, shaping combat basics, oaths, cold-wrought iron), it contains a universal, non-Grace-gated Assumption-type Charm tree (the gateway shinma Nirakara, 'the Mask') plus five per-Grace Charm trees, each opened by prose describing its shinma and closed or interleaved with combat-mechanics sections (shaping attack/soak/wound-penalty rules for that Grace) that were already summarized at the mechanical-overview level in shaping-combat-basics. Across three passes, this inventory has now fully covered three of the five: the Heart Grace tree (shinma Nirguna, pp. 155-159/PDF 156-160 -- Name Charms, Bedlam-Influencing Charms [notable for drawing branches from all five Graces rather than just Heart], Dodge Charms, Resistance Charms), the Staff Grace tree (shinma Nirvikalpa, pp. 193-196/PDF 194-197 -- the 10-Charm 'Laughing Monster Style' combat tree plus the separate 2-Charm 'Society-Forging Charms' tree, Oath Gossamer and Eight-Corner Ring Binding), and the Cup Grace tree (shinma Dharma, pp. 159-171/PDF 160-172 -- 48 Charms across Cup Combat Charms [including the named 'Spirit-Twisting Obsession Style' sub-tree], Feeding Charms, Addiction Charms, World-Shaping Charms and Virtue-Shaping Charms). The Cup tree and this pass's continuation into the Ring tree both surfaced several Charms that are explicitly gated on a different Grace than the section they sit in (e.g. Beguilement and Spite-Summoning Malediction, Cup-tree Charms explicitly marked 'Minimum Staff' and 'This is a Staff-shaping Charm'; Undetectable Lie, a Ring Combat Charm with the same pattern) -- the same cross-Grace-crossover pattern already flagged for the Heart tree's Bedlam-Influencing Charms, now confirmed as a recurring structural feature of this Charm material rather than a one-off. This pass also began the Ring Grace tree (shinma Nirvishesha, pp. 171-192/PDF 172-193 -- by far the largest of the five), completing only its first named sub-section, Ring Combat Charms (16 Charms, pp. 171-175/PDF 172-176, with two independent roots converging at Sorrowful Firmament Resonance). The rest of the Ring tree (All-Consuming God-Monster Style, Body-Strengthening Charms, Creation-Based Crafting, and a large Glamour Charms section including the 'Forging the (Grace) Grace' Charms that let raksha grant Grace Traits to Creation-born characters and the Freehold-anchoring Forging the Stronghold/Glory/Fountainhead/Throne Room Charms) and the Sword tree (Nishkriya, pp. 196-203/PDF 197-204) remain for future passes, in that page order.

A short, apparently sixth Grace called 'the Way' (shinma Nirupadhika) surfaces on p. 212 (PDF 213), immediately before Chapter Six begins, with a 'Forging the Way Grace' Charm and a 'Perfect Reckoning Technique' Charm. It postdates and sits outside the five Graces (Cup/Ring/Staff/Sword/Heart) established in Chapter Four's Traits chapter and used throughout this inventory's character-creation and Grace rows; it has not been inventoried or cross-referenced against the existing five-Grace model and needs dedicated review (likely alongside Glamour Sorcery, Wyld Artifacts, Adjurations and Behemoths, which immediately precede it on pp. 205-212/PDF 206-213) before any claims are made about whether it is a real player-facing sixth Grace, an artifact/enchantment category, or setting-specific NPC material.
